subject: Request: runtime telemetry visibility + data retention ask
messages:
From: Emma Smith <emma@acadiahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acadiahealth.com
Date: 2028-03-07T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Request: runtime telemetry visibility + data retention ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acadia is excited about Redwood's performance profile. Procurement asked me to share a DPA redline and an ask from our privacy team: they want us to retain runtime telemetry (latency + request/response hashes for debugging) for 180 days rather than your standard 30 days. They also ask that telemetry exports to analytics vendors be explicitly permitted in an exhibit.

I attached the redline (Acadia-DPA-redline-v3.docx) and a diagram of the telemetry pipeline (runtime-telemetry-diagram.png). Helpful context: we need the longer retention for our clinical QA audits and incident reconstruction; they say 180d is the minimum.

Can Redwood sign this retention extension and add an exhibit that enumerates allowable telemetry exports (we can propose vendor list after you confirm the model)? If not, can we get a documented exception path and a runbook for sensitive-data masking in traces?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — legal is targeting contract signoff by 3/20.

Best,
Emma Smith
Senior Procurement Manager
Acadia Health

Hi Emma — thanks for the detailed note and the redline. Looping in product (Lauren) and security (Olga) plus Dev for legal/ops implications. A few quick clarifying questions so we can route this internally:

- Which telemetry fields are required for the 180d retention ask? Is this full request/response bodies, or hashed/metadata-only?
- Does Acadia require exports to be automated to external analytics vendors, or just the option to export on-demand for incident investigations?
- Are there specific analytics vendors to be listed in the exhibit now, or can we treat that as a post-signature punchlist?

Initial position from my side: Redwood's default retention for runtime traces is 30 days to limit exposure and minimize PII risks. We can consider an exception path for PG&E-style enterprise customers with strong contractual controls (contractual encryption at rest, access controls, and audit logs). If Acadia is asking for 180d, we need to scope it down (hashed request/response metadata only) and add strong masking rules plus a telemetry export whitelist rather than an open export.

OLGA / LAUREN — can you weigh in on the security compliance and product feasibility? If we can agree on a mitigated retention profile (hashed IDs + request metadata only), I can ask legal to draft an exhibit and a runbook for the exception.

Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: runtime telemetry visibility + data retention ask

Karthik / team / Emma — quick security assessment and requested clarifications from my side: 

1) Scope of data: we cannot accept full request/response bodies retained 180d without strong contractual and technical controls. A compensating control approach we can evaluate:
   - Persist only hashed request identifiers, timestamps, latency metrics, model-id, and error codes for 180d.
   - Persist raw responses for 30d by default; extend raw retention only if data is pseudonymized and customer-provided tokenization is used.

2) Subprocessor/export controls: any outbound export to analytics vendors must be enumerated in an exhibit. We can include a managed-vendor list as an appendix and add a defined process to add vendors (procurement + security signoff). We will not agree to an unbounded clause that permits exports to unnamed third parties.

3) Operational guardrails: before granting an exception, we require:
   - KMS-based encryption with separate key access per-tenant (or documented equivalent if customer manages keys).
   - Role-based access controls and audit logs for all telemetry access.
   - A documented incident reconstruction runbook that limits human access and uses noise-injection for rare sensitive tokens.

4) Legal redlines that will be non-starters without compensation or SLA tradeoffs: unlimited retention of identifiable PII, vendor export without approvals, and obligations that would require Redwood to re-identify hashed data.

Recommended next steps (internal + to Acadia):
- Product to confirm which telemetry fields can be hashed/pseudonymized (Lauren).
- Dev to confirm feasibility of tenant-keyed encryption and access logging (Dev).
- If product/security accept mitigations, Legal (Karthik) to propose an Exhibit A with the vendor whitelist and a telemetry retention table.

Emma — if Acadia can accept the hashed/metadata-only approach for 180d and vendor whitelist process, that would head off the biggest concerns from security. Otherwise we should discuss a shorter raw-data retention plus a documented, auditable export process.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick product take and action items.

Product position: we can support the proposed mitigated profile with these concrete limits: 
- 180d retention limited to hashed request identifiers, latency metrics, model id, status codes, and truncated error traces (no raw user content).
- Raw request/response bodies: 30d default. Extension to raw bodies only via Ops-run export for incident response with manual approvals.
- Exports: allowed only to enumerated vendors listed in Exhibit A; additions to the list require a three-party approval (Acadia procurement + Redwood security + Redwood product).

Action items: 
1) Dev to confirm psuedo-prod feasibility for tenant-keyed encryption at rest and per-tenant audit logs (Dev: can you confirm ETA?).
2) Karthik to engage Legal and draft Exhibit A template and the retention table for the DPA (Karthik: please provide initial draft by 3/13 if possible).
3) Olga to review the draft exhibit and provide final security language.
4) Emma / Acadia to confirm whether they accept hashed/metadata-only 180d or will push for raw 180d.

If we align on the mitigated profile I will prioritize a product task to expose a telemetry toggle per-account (off by default) and a management console flag for export requests. That will be on our roadmap for Q2 but we can also backstop manually for Acadia as an enterprise exception.

Thanks — Lauren
